summary: Counter counts hashable items into a dictionary-like collection.
documentation: Counter counts hashable items into a dictionary-like collection. Counts can be read by item, and constructing it from an iterable counts each occurrence. Missing keys read as zero without inserting them.
inputs: An iterable of hashable values, or a mapping of counts.
returns: A Counter mapping items to counts.
caution: Construction from a mapping treats values as counts. This task supplies a list, and keys must be hashable.
scenarios: Summarize item-name frequencies in an order list.
Count response categories in a survey export.
Build a distribution of status labels from a local log.
title: Count request categories
problem: Input is a list of category strings. Return a plain dictionary mapping each distinct exact string to its frequency. Treat case differences and an empty string as distinct categories.
goal: Use collections.Counter or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Import Counter from collections, then convert its result to dict.
